page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector calculations and deep learning inference workloads. Cryptographic operations are aided by hardware-accelerated AES instructions.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfc7.2xlarge in the average performance tier for general computing. It achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1319.0 and a multi-core score of 5101.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read speed of 56.48 GB/sec and a write speed of 39.57 GB/sec for large blocks. While it handles small-model LLM inference efficiently, performance drops significantly on larger models, with a 7B parameter model yielding only 6.26 tokens/sec during text generation. This hardware profile is optimized for compute-heavy workloads such as web serving, software compilation, and database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks local storage, relying instead on network-attached storage. The processor supports AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI instructions, enhancing vector and cryptographic performance. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute tasks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 5101.0 and a static web serving throughput of 8.02 GB/sec. However, it exhibits limitations in demanding workloads like medium-parameter LLM inference. This instance is best suited for high-frequency compute tasks, software compilation, web serving, and database operations requiring dedicated CPU resources without massive memory footprints.
